utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution had a preliminary matter to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and good morning. If we could briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Simovic. Before you give evidence, the rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the text of which is now handed out to you. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simovic. Please be seated. Mr. Simovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic, and you'll find him to your left, is a member of the Mladic Defence team. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can have in e-court the document with the 65 ter number 1D01656. And while we are waiting, perhaps a clean hard copy can be given to the witness, with the assistance of the usher. And now we have the first page up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you look at the signature on this first page of this statement and tell me if you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can now turn to the last page of the statement in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whose signature this is?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, after signing this statement for the Defence team of General Mladic, did you have occasion to review the same in the Serbian language in order to verify if there were any corrections necessary?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you in proofing advise me of certain clarifications or corrections?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could first turn to page 2 of the statement in both languages, and I'd like to focus on paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When talking of the wedding party that was attacked in Sarajevo, did have you any clarifications you wished to make there?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. What is written here is that members of a Serb wedding party were killed. It was one member of a Serb wedding party that was killed, not several, as is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could look at paragraph 5 on the same page, do you have any clarifications that you'd like to make in respect to this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead and tell us what those clarifications are.

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, some words have been inserted here, and therefore this paragraph becomes senseless. As far as I know, in April 1992 or thereabouts, the Crisis Staff was formed in the Foca municipality. The Muslims from Donje Polje near Foca were the first to fire at the Serbian population. I would kindly ask Their Honours for the following. I mean, these refugees who were here, what followed, you see this which continues, it continues, and it says, persons arrived in Foca. They were refugees from Konjic and Sarajevo; i.e., from those areas that had a predominantly Muslim population. If "as a result" is to be taken out, when Muslims from Donje Polje who were the first to open fire at the Serbian population, refugees from Konjic and Sarajevo, and that's 200 kilometres away from Foca, and that is impossible. So it all doesn't make sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Halfway the answer I heard I would kindly ask Their Honours. Was that text spoken by our interpreters or was it by the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness. The witness addressed the Court directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just so we could be clear, sir, are you saying then, if I understand line 15 of page 4 correctly, you would like the words "as a result" to be removed from this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. "As a result," yes, that should be deleted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page in both languages. And if we could focus on paragraph number 12 and Mr. Malis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What would you like to say about this paragraph to clarify the same?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is what it says there. I remember that one time a military police officer, Malis, who was a military police commander from the VRS came to Foca.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness. Other microphones are on and there is too much background noise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please slowly repeat your answer? And could all unnecessary microphones be switched off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that one time a military police officer, Malis, who was a military police commander from the VRS, came to Foca. All of this is put the other way around, these words. Malis was appointed commander of the military police of the Army of Republika Srpska when the army was being established. He did not come from Sarajevo. He came to Foca. He became commander of the military police there and he stayed on there, whereas what is written here is: "I did not see him but I heard that he came in order to resolve the issue of those individuals," that's to say that he was there and he stayed and he didn't go anywhere. And here, if it says "I remember that one time Malis came," et cetera, Malis was appointed a military police officer of the VRS in Foca. He came there and stayed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, apart from these clarifications that we've gone through in court today, do you otherwise stand by everything that is recorded in your written statement as being accurate and not needing any correction?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I were to ask you questions based on the same topics as contained in your written statement today, would your answers to those questions be the same in substance as we find in your written statement?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And given that today you have taken the solemn declaration to tell the truth, would those answers, as recorded in your statement, be truthful?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence would move at this time that 1D01656 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Witness, could you tell us what Mr. Mladic is charged with in the indictment in relation to Foca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The general is charged with the commission of some crimes in Foca, and I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What crimes? Could you tell us? Which ones specifically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But in your statement we read that you are not familiar with the circumstances of incidents charged, but if you do not know what the incidents are, how could you tell us that you're unfamiliar with it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because in Foca, in my opinion, sir, there weren't any crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of people being detained in KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you may have some knowledge on detention, which is relevant for this case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, from about people who were detained at the KP Dom, people who were detained were persons who were taken prisoner in war operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you have an opinion about what happened in KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, on what basis did you say that you have no knowledge about these incidents, if you do not know what the incidents are? Did anyone tell you or did you read the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Mr. President, I'm a soldier. I just did what a serving soldier is supposed to do. Documents were not accessible to me and I could not read that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your statement that you have no knowledge or you're unfamiliar with the circumstances is, if you again -- if you have no knowledge about what they are, is a rather senseless statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand the question very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you say I'm not familiar with the circumstances of the incidents, that is a rather senseless statement if you do not know what the incidents were, isn't it? That's my question, whether you agree with me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what kind of incidents we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, in your statement, you say that you're not familiar with the circumstances of those incidents. Now, if you do not know what incidents we are talking about, then that doesn't make much sense, not to know about something you do not know what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. Those incidents -- those incidents, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1656 receives number D583, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D583 is admitted. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. At this time I would read a public summary of the statement, the purpose of which has been explained to the witness during proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The witness's statement details that even before April 1992, barricades were set up in Foca town. In Muslim villages, the posting of guards was widespread and the guards moved around villages and could be seen carrying guns. Fearing that preparations were underway to wipe out the Serbian population from the area, the local Serbs organised themselves locally through the Territorial Defence to defend their homes. The Muslims were the first to fire at the Serbian population from Donje Polje. Before the establishment of the VRS, all the people organised themselves in accordance with Territorial Defence principles and the Foca Crisis Staff had de facto power. In addition to the tactical group in Foca, the witness says there were various armed groups and individuals that were not under anyone's control. They operated independently and clashed with people in Foca. The witness know that is a VRS military police commander came to Foca to try and resolve the issue of these individuals. The witness never received an unlawful order nor heard of any such orders and that completes the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have any further questions to the witness, please put them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, now I'd like to go through other parts of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 2 in both languages, I would like to start with paragraph number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in this paragraph, you say: "I knew something evil was afoot, that things would no longer be the same. There were opinions that preparations were under way to wipe out the Serbian population from the area." What was the bases of these conclusions or concerns that you had?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said. That is my opinion. I spent a lot of time in Sarajevo over that last year, practically I spent every weekend in Sarajevo. I saw Green Berets walking about town, in a state, based on the rule of law, the Patriotic League, the speech of Sulejman Ugljanin in at a rally in Foca saying that he would come to Foca with 50.000 fierce Sandzakli and resolve the matter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not catch the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: We were not organised --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you resume from where you said that you -- when you talked about the speech indicating that 50.000 fierce Sandzaklije would come to Foca and resolve the matter. Could you repeat from there on your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honour. At the rally in Foca, this was a SDA rally in Foca, Sulejman Ugljanin, president of the SDA for Sandzak, said he would bring in 50.000 fierce Sandzakli to resolve the matter, that Foca of 1942 would not be repeated. All of these things that I'm talking about now were noticed in a big village, predominantly Muslim populated. I as a citizen of the then Yugoslavia, I just wore blue jeans and I stated that because that's what I thought. We had nothing, we just had a T-shirt on, and they have paramilitary formations, Green Berets, the Patriotic League, they have 50.000 Sandzakli. They have guards around the town of Foca. And that's why I said if war were to break out, and I hoped that war would not break out, we would not be left. We could not survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, if we can take you -- look together at paragraph 7 of your statement, should be on the same page in both versions, here you identify that you joined the 5th Battalion on or about 15 April 1992. Was this 5th Battalion part of the VRS or some other formation at the time that you joined?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: The 5th Battalion was within the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did that 5th Battalion later become part of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at the time that you were a member of the Territorial Defence or later the VRS, were you ever instructed on the laws of war and how to deal with civilians and prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we had this issue Friday as well. This is a witness who is testifying as an exception to the agreement that only witnesses who had previously testified would be called before the summer recess because of late disclosure of all the Defence statements. Perhaps I've missed it, but is the instruction on the law of war covered in the witness's statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I do think it arises out of paragraph 13 where he says I never saw or heard anything unlawful was done in the formation that he joined, so I think for that paragraph to have meaning we do have to ascertain what the witness was told, if he was instructed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But instructions and what happens are two different things, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by what happens, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if I say that I never committed a traffic offence, it doesn't say anything about my training as a driver. Of course, you can link everything to everything but at least it's not clear that this is part of the -- that this is part of the statement. Mr. Traldi, it seems not to be so dramatic as to invite Mr. Ivetic to stop at this moment, but I do understand that you wanted to put on the record that Mr. Ivetic's opinion about what is covered by the statement and your opinion are quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think that's an accurate characterisation, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, at the time that you were a member of the Territorial Defence or later the VRS, were you ever instructed on the laws of war and how to deal with civilians and prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what is it that you were instructed?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Every unit of the Territorial Defence and later on of the Army of Republika Srpska had this order that was standing up there, and every soldier could read it and it was read many times before a lineup of soldiers and this is how it read, I quote -- maybe I'm not going to quote it exactly verbatim because it was 20 years ago, but I will quote at least some of the words from that order. "I hereby order all officers, NCOs, and soldiers of Republika Srpska to behave in accordance with the Geneva Conventions." And then underneath it said: "I hereby forbid the torching and destruction of movable and immovable property." Number 2: "The maltreatment of the civilian population. "Enemy soldiers and the wounded should be assisted. Soldiers who are taken prisoner should be treated with dignity." There were other orders too, but Your Honours I cannot remember now. It's been 20 years after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you identify a Dragan Nikolic Intervention Unit. Can you please tell us what this unit was?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is a unit that the Territorial Defence established as the military police. Its aim was to protect the Serb and Muslim population during war operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And why was this unit called the Dragan Nikolic Intervention Unit? Who was Dragan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Nikolic was the first commander of that unit, and he was killed in the clashes with the Muslim forces in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you have been recorded as saying this was a unit of the Territorial Defence established as a military police with the aim to protect the Serb and Muslim population during war operations. How was that aim to be accomplished?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I did not quite understand this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. How did the Dragan Nikolic Intervention Unit act to try to protect the Serb and Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they came, I mean if somebody would report that there had been maltreatment of the Serb population, they acted in accordance with the law. They took them to the KP Dom regardless of who this was, a Serb or a Muslim or a Croat, regardless of religion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in paragraphs 7 to 8 of your statement, you talk about paramilitaries. Where did these paramilitaries come from?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, a paramilitary formation of about 70 men arrived in -- from Serbia, they called themselves the Black Eagles. There was this other unit that came from Montenegro consisting of about 35 men. Many people came at the time, but I remember these units very well, these two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What were these various paramilitary units doing in Foca town?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to present my opinion. They brought shame and disgrace to the honest combatants of Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at paragraph 9 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- you talk about how they provoked incidents and came into conflict with the civilian population. What can you tell us about the interactions between the paramilitaries and the civilian authorities in Foca?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, there may and translation issue but I didn't see any reference to "civilian population."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise. It says "population."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, what can you tell us about the interactions between the paramilitaries and the civilian authorities in Foca?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself have any personal encounters with the paramilitaries, and if so, can you explain the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This too I think goes beyond the witness's statement. Also, it was not contained in any proofing note or anything. And based on our agreement and the limited exception we've granted in this case, I'm just concerned that a necessity to recall the witness may arise if this line of questioning is going to go into much detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe it arises out of paragraph 11. Let me rephrase my question to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 11 of your statement, sir, you say about these undisciplined volunteers that could not be brought under control: "They were told that they had to place themselves under control but they refused this." Were you present when this was communicated to these individuals?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you explain first the circumstances of how you came to be present when this was communicated to these group of undisciplined volunteers or paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I was about 20 kilometres away from Foca. I was summoned there by the commander of the 5th Battalion. He told me, and I quote, "Simovic take ten men with you, go into town, report to the commander of the military police, and you will receive instructions there. The criminals from Belgrade seem to have started causing problems again." I took ten soldiers with me. I went there, reported to the military police, and about 50 of us soldiers went to that area where they were stationed. The military police commander said, "If you don't place yourself under our control, you have two hours to leave. To get lost." And they did not like it, they said that they had come here to fight for the Serb people, one of them in the front ranks was saying something, and I said to him because I was standing, there "you came here not to fight but to loot, to rob people. And the orders that I had received were that we should kill them if they filed obey. They saw this group of 50 soldiers positioned a bit further up, and I was standing there right in front of them. They said, "We will leave, we will not work according to your rules, we will leave but we will come back. You killed one of our soldiers and we will avenge him." And then I quote myself, I said, "Leave, and if you come again, we will be here waiting for you."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And lastly I'd like to focus on paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could I ask, you were ordered to kill them if they would not obey. You didn't fulfil that order, is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not obey this order because the order was that if they refused to leave the town, we were to kill them, but if they left, obviously the order did not apply any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to focus on paragraph 12 where you've identified a military police officer, Malis. Can you give us some details about what he did to try to resolve the issue of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 30th of June 1992, the Foca Brigade of the VRS was established. Up until that time we only had the Territorial Defence. Mr. Malis was appointed the commander of the military police, and Dragan Nikolic Detachment received new tasks. I know but I did not see for myself that it was his task to deal with those cases. And after that time, in June, July, I can't recall the exact time, another formation arrived in the town of Foca, probably with the same goal as the previous ones. He was there waiting for them and he told them that they should not be in Foca and that they had only enough time to pack their things and go. I know that they fired on his car and three of those men were arrested and taken to the KP Dom. And now as to seven or eight other people who were there, they disappeared, they just fled, and they never came back into town again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, on behalf of my client and team I thank you for answering my questions. That completes the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Traldi before you start your cross-examination, I'd like to put a few short questions to the witness. Witness, do you have any knowledge where you said you only had blue jeans and nothing else, did you have any knowledge about Serbs being armed and weapons being distributed among Serbs in the Foca area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't quite understand your question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said I was in blue jeans, we had nothing, and that's -- you explained that in the context of the organisation, the military organisation, of the Muslims. My question to you is: Do you have any knowledge about the distribution of weapons among the Serbs and/or Serbs being armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My second question is: Have you ever arrested someone as a prisoner of war? You or your unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us the details?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the course of many combat operations, we fought the enemy soldiers on many occasions, and we would sometimes capture them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you do with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have already said, we had the standing order that the prisoners of war, those should be treated with dignity regardless of the fact that they were the enemy. That's what I had said. The Supreme Command issued this order. We had to treat them in line with the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us one example of a person being taken prisoner of war and what you did with them -- with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm a soldier. We would capture their soldiers -- well, it is my estimates more or less --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stop you there. I'm asking for one specific example.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you're asking me about what happened when we would capture them. My duty, when an enemy soldier was captured, was to treat them properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stop you again. I'm asking for you for one specific example, where, who, when.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. I do apologise. Let me give you an example. There was a clash at Treskavica. We had to take an elevation which was of great strategic importance for both sides. We captured about 18 Muslim fighters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometime in 1993, 1994. I think it was in late 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, do you have any example of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you ever visited KP Dom in Foca? In, well let's say, in April, May, June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about who were detained there? And I'm asking about personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you couldn't tell us exactly who, then, were detained there, whether these were prisoners of war, whether they were criminals, whether they were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I don't know what happened in KP Dom. As a soldier, I did not have the right to even go there. I think that for the most part, the soldiers who fired on us were imprisoned there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm interested in your personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about the KP Dom in Foca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Mr. Traldi, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed. Mr. Simovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. You'll find him to your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're a member of a war veterans association, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Have you held a position in that association?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What position?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm the president of the war veterans association in one of the local boards in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You signed your statement on the 8th of June this year. Where did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: In the veterans association.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Was anyone else there, aside from members of the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: The secretary. She works there at the veterans association.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions about the evidence that you've just provided this morning. Did you inform the Defence that you had personal interactions with members of paramilitary forces in Foca?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I did not quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll rephrase. Did you inform any member of the Defence team that you, yourself, had personally interacted with members of Serb paramilitary forces, met with them and told them to leave, as you described this morning?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As to that meeting that you testified about this morning, when did it take place? At what point in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: It happened in front of the sports hall in Foca because this paramilitary unit was stationed in the Foca secondary school. We came there and we conveyed this order that they should leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps the question was unclear in some way but I asked you at what point in 1992, what month, if you know, that meeting occurred, not where it occurred. So do you recall what month in 1992 that meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: No. It's been 20 years, sir. And some things got a bit mixed up in my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You said the paramilitaries had brought shame and disgrace on honest combatants in Foca. How did they do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that was at temporary transcript page 14.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we called them the dogs of war. They did not have any ideals. They had nothing. Their main objective was to make money. I consider them as criminals. Well, it was not just me. They actually were criminals. They simply wanted to make money, and they did not care about the means. They maltreated the population, not only Muslims. They maltreated Serbs as well. And then we had had enough and they had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, at temporary transcript page 7 today, lines 7 and 8, you testified: "... in Foca, in my opinion, sir, there weren't any crimes." Is what you're saying now that in fact there were crimes committed in 1992 in Foca?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I was talking about those criminals robbing and maltreating, not only the Muslims but the Serbs as well. Their main goal was to get hold of some money and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So just to be perfectly clear and precise, you don't stand by your evidence that there were no crimes committed by armed Serb forces in Foca in 1992. You're now testifying there were crimes, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we get a reference for that? I think it misstates the prior evidence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps literally put to the witness the portion you're referring to, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I just referred to it and he said in my -- in Foca in 1992 in my opinion there were no crimes, which I would submit is -- covers crimes by all sorts of people. It's at transcript page 7, lines 7 and 8, Mr. President, you asked him about his knowledge of the incidents charged in the indictment and the specific language he used was: "Because in Foca, in my opinion, sir, there weren't any crimes." So I'm putting to him that his now is inconsistent with that testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And he's expanding it by talking now about other crimes apart from those that were charged in the indictment which was the subject of Your Honour's interchange with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the statement of the witness was of a rather general nature, although the question was focused on crimes in the indictment that -- but that's the reason I take it why you want to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. President. And given that the witness also testified he wasn't aware what crimes were charged in the indictment, I didn't understand that it was possible his answer could have been limited to those crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, you're allowed to explore the matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, to reiterate my question, your evidence now is there were crimes committed by armed Serb forces in 1992 in Foca, correct?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Your Honour, Mr. Prosecutor, I perhaps misunderstood you. You were asking me about whether there were any crimes, and you were not asking me about offences, criminal offences. If you say criminal offence, what I mean by that is if you burn a house, if you slap somebody, and I think that they were going around slapping people, torching houses, I did not see that, I heard that from other citizens. I perhaps misunderstood you. You asked me whether there any crimes in 1992. I perhaps just misunderstood you. You did not ask me about criminal offences. A criminal offence for me is a mistreating an enemy soldier, torch a house, slap somebody during the war regardless of their religion. I consider that to be a criminal offence. And I'm sure that there were such offences committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And as I understood your evidence a moment ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As I understood your evidence a moment ago, you're aware that such offences were committed by Serb forces in Foca, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, it misstates the prior testimony of this witness. Can I get a ruling on that objection, finally?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you understand English, Witness? Do you understand the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please take off your ear-phones for a second? Mr. Ivetic, could you further explain in what respect it misstates the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Twice now, the Prosecution counsel has said that this witness has linked crimes to Serb forces. Which is not what this -- the witness has said. I'd asked for a ruling on that objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now it's clear. I understood the reference to the repeated mentioning of Serb paramilitary forces, which are Serb forces, Mr. Ivetic. If you don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you change -- if it's Serb paramilitary, then it's Serb paramilitary. If it's Serb forces, that's changing it to mean something different, more general, because Serb forces can also mean other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No. No. Serb paramilitary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That -- that objection is denied. We understand the explanation of the witness was Serb military forces. Mr. Traldi, it would have been advisable to continue to use that wording, but Serb paramilitary forces are still Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, you see my -- you see the point of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now Your Honour has just said Serb military forces in line 16 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- which is an entirely different matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You did. You just said it. There is a chance of confusion, that's why I'm asking for the Prosecution to be very precise and stick to what is the evidence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I meant to say that those were armed forces when I said military forces. I think I misstated the question put by Mr. Traldi earlier. He had talked about armed forces. Mr. Traldi, it would be advisable to connect your question to what the witness said, and I apologise for having used the word "military" where I intended to use the word armed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's time for the break anyhow. Witness, "Svedok," Witness, we will take a break of 20 minutes. We would like to see you back after the break. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 5 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to return to the last question I was asking before the break, sir, it's correct, isn't it, that it is not your opinion that no crimes were committed in Foca, but that you are personally aware that Serb paramilitary forces committed crimes against non-Serbs in Foca; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know about crimes. What I do know is that criminal acts, criminal offences, were committed, but crimes are a different matter. They were robbing people, they would enter a house, rob everything and then set it on fire. That's a criminal offence, as far as I'm concerned, and it is up to this Tribunal to decide whether it was also a crime or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll move on and I won't insist on the terminology for the moment. Turning to another point from your testimony this morning, you testified about a speech which claimed -- in which it was claimed that 50.000 people from Sandzak were going to be sent to Foca. Now I just have one question about this. That never happened, did it?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I want to turn to the structure of your own forces. You state in paragraph 13 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- that your commander was Marko Kovac. He was the commander of the Foca Tactical Group, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, I know that Marko Kovac was the commander of the Foca Brigade which was part of the Republika Srpska army. Now, as for this tactical group, I don't really know what it means. I don't know what it was established. What I do know is that Marko Kovac was the commander of the Foca Brigade which was established -- I know that because I'm a member of the war veterans association. It was established in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So he became your commander in June of 1992, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And by that time, you'd already transferred into the Dragan Nikolic Intervention Unit, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 13 that Colonel Kovac was your commander. Now, your unit's immediate commander was Brane Cosovic, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But your unit received orders from Colonel Kovac, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Colonel Kovac reported on your detachment's activities to his superior command, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to look at just one example of such a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 30982.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, what we are seeing here is a report from Colonel Kovac dated the 2nd of August 1992. And -- which is -- appears to have been sent to the Herzegovina Corps command from the Foca Tactical Group, and it says it was received by a radio link and also refers to the information centre Trebinje. Looking at --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was going to be my point. It appears to be coming from the centre for information in Trebinje rather than from the tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Actually, it says this is a regular Foca Tactical Group report received by radio link. It says it comes from Colonel Kovac. And, Your Honour, we saw this on another document last week, P6680. It's also the case with P2835, 2839, and 2842 which have all been admitted, so it appears from the documents in the record that this was not an uncommon channel of communications for the Foca Tactical Group. But I'd submit based on what we see here as well as the fact that the document comes from the Herzegovina Corps collection that it's pretty clear who it's being sent to and who it's being sent from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that the Trebinje reference is a reference to what seems to be a transfer by whatever technical means, whereas the content may be not exactly the same; that is, the origin of this specific copy may be -- but let me just have a look -- yes. No, it's not only the -- I see that it's also Trebinje on the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In terms of technical means it is a does say it was received by radio link. It gives a date and a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, apparently you can interpret the origin in various ways and we -- you may proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Looking at point 2, sir, Colonel Kovac is reporting that: "Special Detachments Dragan Nikolic, Zaga, and Elez freed Rogoj inflicting heavily losses on the Ustashas. The remaining TG units repelled the Ustasha attack." Then it reports "losses on our side." "And the Dragan Nikolic Detachment" -- that's your detachment, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He uses Ustashas to describe enemy forces. Was that common in your units?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll rephrase. Colonel Kovac uses the word "Ustashas" to describe enemy forces. Was that commonly used in your unit and the other units with which your unit cooperated, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: The only thing that I do know is that we called the enemy soldiers Ustashas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, he refers to Rogoj. The Rogoj pass is an important strategic feature, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's important, among other things, to control over the route from Sarajevo to Foca?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He's reporting that your detachment took part in this action. Did you also take part in it yourself?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I take it to -- from your answer to Mr. President's question earlier, to the best of your knowledge your detachment did not take any prisoners during this operation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 30982.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30982 receives number P6684, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you now a few questions about the detachment. Where was your detachment headquartered?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: In a room in the Zelengora Hotel in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What neighbourhood was that in?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, Radomir Kovac was a member of your unit, correct?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: His nickname was Klanfa?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In the last document, we saw that your unit engaged in operations together with the Zaga detachment. Its commander was Dragomir Kunarac, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I know only his nickname, Zaga, I don't know his full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, that detachment included some fighters from Montenegro, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was based at a house called 16 Ulica Osmana Dikica. I apologise for my pronunciation but hopefully it shows up correctly for you. That's correct, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Were you ever there yourself?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kunarac has been convicted at this Tribunal for crimes in Foca including crimes against women committed at that house. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment, I did not know what this unit called Zaga was doing. None of the superiors knew [Realtime transcript read in error "this appears new"], but it did turn out that this man was sentenced before this Tribunal. I don't know what sentence he received but I would like, if you allow me, to express my opinion of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All I'd asked was whether you were aware that he'd been convicted. And I take it from your answer, you were. It's clear from the last document, that his unit, like yours, was receiving orders from Colonel Kovac, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So this wasn't one of the detachments that wasn't under anyone's control? This was a detachment that was under the control of the Foca Brigade or the Foca Tactical Group, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We also just saw in the same document that your unit engaged in operations together with the Elez Battalion, that's a battalion commanded by Pero Elez, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's the Miljevina Battalion or the 7th Battalion, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And one of his men was Radovan Stankovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: His nickname was Rasa?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: By sight only.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, are you aware that Mr. Stankovic has been convicted in Bosnia of crimes in Foca, including crimes against women committed at a place called Karaman's house in Miljevina?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about any crimes in Miljevina. I do know that he was sentenced before this Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Kovac, who we mentioned earlier, from your unit, he lived in the Lepa Brena Block of apartments in Foca, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it Dragomir or is it Marko?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, Radomir Kovac from your unit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: From --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- he lived in the Lepa Brena apartments in Foca, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Somewhere there, around the centre. I'm not sure where they lived but somewhere around the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And were you ever at the place where he lived in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're aware, too, aren't you, that Mr. Kovac has been convicted before this Tribunal of crimes in Foca including crimes against women committed in his apartment, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I did not know about these crimes. Most probably they were committed but our superiors didn't know about that, most probably. That is something that was strictly prohibited to us as soldiers. This Kovac returned to town, and I said that I would never have let him go, had I been asked, that they had not sentenced had him to a strict enough sentence. I mean, knowing our superiors. I mean, what he did disgraced me as a soldier, disgraced my officers, my commanders. I said that to him personally, to his face. He is in town. I said, if I were your judge, you would have been on the electric chair and I wouldn't have pressed the button once but several times. I can tell you that no superiors knew about his crimes, say not 70 but 95 per cent of all soldiers were --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think the last part of your answer may not have been recorded, 95 per cent of all soldiers were what, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Nothing else was said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to say that soldiers like he brought disgrace on all the honourable soldiers of the town of Foca and our officers, they did not respect the command. Had I been asked, I told him that to his face, and I can square here before God, I said to him, "You fared well. Had I been your judge, I would have taken you to the electric chair and I would have pressed the button three times, not once," because he brought disgrace upon me as a warrior. He did not follow the orders of our superior officers, and he brought shame and disgrace on all the honourable combatants of the Army of Republika Srpska and the general. Such combatants like Kovac. It wasn't just like that that he was sentenced before this Court. But knowing our superiors, how rigorous they were in terms of such measures, this must have been done secretly. Knowing Commander Branimir Cosovic, had we know about these crimes I swear by God before this Court, I would have been his judge and executioner even if I'd never leave prison after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I can see you have strong feelings about Mr. Kovac's crimes. I just have two specific questions about the answer you've just provided. The first one, you testified earlier that paramilitaries had brought shame and disgrace on the honourable VRS combatants in Foca municipality. It wasn't just paramilitaries. It was also some of the members of the VRS who brought disgrace on the others by committing crimes, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And second, I appreciate your opinion of Commander Cosovic, but you don't personally know what he was or wasn't aware of about Mr. Kovac's crimes in 1992, do you?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, but knowing the gentleman, my commander, knowing how many times he told us that we should not do anything wrong in terms of the code of war, I cannot say anything. But I did not notice, but I did not see, because knowing my commander, knowing his character, knowing my officers, knowing my generals, had we known, again, I swear before God, I believe in God -- and I believe in God, and he served his sentence, the one that The Hague Tribunal imposed on him, and there must have been a reason for that. Had I known, had we known about what happened -- I'm sorry, I got carried away by my emotions, but he will face the judgement of God, like everyone else. He fared the way he did here on earth and now how he will fare before the face of God, let that be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He wasn't punished during the war by his commanders, was he?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, Mr. Prosecutor, I said just now that we in the unit did not know what he was committing these crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, I mentioned several people convicted after the war from VRS units in Foca. None of them were punished during the war for the crimes they had committed either by their commanders or by the military courts, were they?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Could you just explain this question to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. And I'll make it a little bit more specific. I mentioned Mr. Stankovic, Mr. Kunarac, Mr. Kovac. They were all convicted after the war. They were all members of VRS units in Foca during the war. None of them were punished during the war either by their commanders or by the military courts for the crimes they committed; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Had we known that they had done this -- well, it probably hadn't reached our superiors. However, had it reached them, because I mean for somebody to do something like this, of course they would have to do it in secret, because mistreating the civilian population was strictly forbidden. That order was hanging on the wall. They violated that. I did not know, and I believe that my commander didn't know either. I believe that my superiors did not know about that either. They were rigorous. These people must have done this in secret. That's why I said that people like this, what do I call them? I mean in public here before this Court, these soulless beings, they brought disgrace on me, on the Army of Republika Srpska. As for these three men that I see here, you cannot say that all the fighters from Foca and that our command are the same like these three. I beg your pardon. I mean, I said what I said. I said this to the public prosecutor. I apologise to the Judges if they misunderstood this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Aside from them, no other members of your unit were punished during the war for wrongful facts they may have committed against Muslims, were they?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: These three were not punished. Again I'm saying we did not know. We did not know about their offences. Believe me, we punished soldiers when we knew about the violations of orders, say as far as the cease-fire was concerned. Sometimes they would be sentenced to two months, whatever, for this kind of crime. They would have been held accountable by our command, had our command known about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn now to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, may I put one question in relation to this topic you have dealt with. Mr. Witness, I would like to take you back to your evidence about Mr. Kunarac, on page 31, line 20 and 21. You said: "At that moment I did not know what this unit called Zaga was doing." And I understood the next sentence to be none of his superiors knew. It is wrongly recorded, but this is what I heard. Do I repeat your answer correctly? None of his superiors knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When I said -- well, I'm sorry, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Let me put --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Didn't know then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Let me put my question to you: How do you know that no -- none of the superiors of Mr. Kunarac know -- knew about crimes committed by him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If any of our superiors knew that he had done that, then he's the same. But our superiors strictly prohibited that kind of thing, and that is why I don't believe that any one of our superiors knew. Well, I cannot say. I was not present during these conversations, but I cannot say that anyone of our superior officers knew about what Kunarac did, in my view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one more question: Do you know of anybody who was punished by your superiors for any crimes that he might have committed? Just say "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn now to the topic of prisoners. You mentioned, at temporary transcript page 19, that your unit had taken a number of prisoners during an operation on Treskavica in 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Where did you bring them?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: We took them to the command. This happened while we were in action, on the ground. I think 22 soldiers were taken prisoner, and they were brought in. We told the military police that they were taken prisoner, and according to establishment, you are supposed to let the military police know so that they would meet these prisoners who are then taken to the KP Dom. The orders I had was that I should inform the military police if I take a prisoner of war and then I hand these prisoners of war over to the military police and then they do their job.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You testified that you hadn't taken prisoners during operations in Foca. Was there a similar standing order that if prisoners were taken they would be taken to the military police and then taken to the KP Dom in Foca?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Not the military police, but all units that take a soldier prisoner were duty-bound to hand this person over to the military police, and then the military police would take that person to the KP Dom or some other institution where these POWs were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence from both Prosecution and Defence witnesses that detainees at KP Dom also included elderly people, women and children. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I did not enter the KP Dom. I mean, we were strictly prohibited from getting close to the KP Dom let alone entering the KP Dom. I'm a soldier and I was supposed to carry out the orders of my superiors. To go to the KP Dom to see who was there, I really don't know. If there were some people -- well, I did not take them prisoner, and I don't belive that we could have taken old men to the KP Dom. I claim that all the persons that we took prisoner, I and my unit, that happened during war operations. I joined later, when the town had fallen. I don't know about these elderly people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's look at 65 ter 14066. Now, this is a list of prisoners of war of Muslim ethnicity being released from KP Dom Foca to be exchanged for captured Serbs. It's dated the 8th of December 1992. I'd ask you to just familiarise yourself with the list for a moment and please say "yes" when you've done so.

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the people being exchanged in this group, looking at the years of birth, are all over 50 years old at the time, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know these people. Now, who brought them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You do see the years of birth and agree with me that at the time they're all recorded to be over 50 years old, though, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And do you see below that, where it says approved by the commander of TG Foca, Mr. Kovac, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that's the stamp for the military post for the Foca Tactical Group, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has shown no knowledge of the persons in the document or the document, so I don't think that the bases for introducing this document through this witness has been met.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would there be any problem in having it admitted from the bar table, Mr. Ivetic? Which is often done if the witness has testified about matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe if the Prosecution wishes to tender documents through the bar table, the procedure to be followed is to a file a submission to allow the Defence to respond. I would ask that that be the way it's done. It was part of your guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My understanding is a little bit different, which is that particularly where a document impeaches evidence directly given by the witness, for instance, in this case his belief that the people in KP Dom Foca were all fighters, then the document can be admitted during cross-examination. This was done during the Prosecution case as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, the Prosecution is misstating the document. First line of the document says "prisoners of war." To be a prisoner of war, one has to be a fighter, so this document does not impeach the witness. It's a mischaracterisation of the highest order.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My submission is that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina is unlikely to have been composed entirely of men over the age of 50 and the ages are suggestive. That's why I focused on them in my questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So, Your Honours, it's not impeaching the witness. It's not presented for that purpose. It's presented for the purpose of presenting the Prosecution's argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, would you agree that your recollection might also relate to documents which are directly linked to the substance of the testimony of the witness, even if it not impeaches him directly?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I would, and I'd argue -- one way of being directly linked, I'd submit, is being indicative of impeachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 14066 receives number P6685, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6685 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we get a ruling from this Chamber: Is it your position that documents are that are indicative of impeachment can be submitted from the bar table by either party?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't get a ruling on that. The document was tendered, both parties have presented their views on the matter, and the objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I get the reasons on the record then for the objection being denied?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider your request, Mr. Ivetic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I want to turn now to some questions about the municipality of Foca itself. Foca was a Muslim-majority municipality before the war, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the interpreters have difficulties in hearing you. Could you come a bit closer to the microphone? And repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honour. To the best of my knowledge in 1991 according to the census, 51 of the -- per cent of the population was the Muslim population and 49 per cent was the Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 02559 B? This is an excerpt from the census. Once it's come up I'll ask for page 2 in the B/C/S. In the English, as we've done in previous instances, we've only translated the column headings rather than asking CLSS to translate the numbers. If we could zoom in at the middle of the page on the heading, "Foca," and I wonder if for ease of reading we might have just the B/C/S version up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, do you see the heading, "Foca"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A little bit further up as well, please, so that we can read the headings of the columns. Yes, there we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So now at the bottom of your screen, do you see the word "Foca"?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if you look straight across to the right, you see that's line 24, correct?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 3 and stay on line 24. And we will again need the column headings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: On the left side, we see Ukupno, roughly total 40.513 of which 20.790 are Muslims, 18.315 Serbs, and relatively small numbers of others. So that's consistent with your recollection that the municipality was about 51 per cent Muslim at the time, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I got my numbers wrong. My opinion was that 51 per cent were Muslims and 49 per cent Serbs. Maybe I made a mistake, but I don't know about these percentages, 23, 18, that's 48.52. That would be my mental math.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I wasn't asking you to do mental math at the moment, sir. What I was suggesting to you, in fact, was that the numbers here are consistent with your recollection and that they are pretty much what you described, 51 per cent Muslims and 49 per cent others. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 02559B receives number P6686, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6686 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, did you notice at any point that most of the Muslims had left Foca?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was not there when the town was taken. My unit joined in at a later stage. I think that a part of the town was liberated, I think, in late March, if I recollect. I know that the Muslim forces in Foca were very strong and most of those forces, when they clashed with our forces, when they realised that they would lose the fight, as we the fighters say, they withdrew towards Ustikolina where there was a Muslim majority population. Quite a few of the honest Muslims were there -- or rather, quite a few of the honest Muslims and their families remained in the town of Foca after their forces withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, even the great majority of the -- of what you're terming honest Muslims left Foca during the war, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you don't mention that in your statement, do you?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: You mean here?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, there.

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence that Serb leaders in Foca -- like Miroslav Stanic, he was the president of the Crisis Staff and then later the war commission, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that's because I think I interrupted myself. Miroslav Stanic was the president of the Crisis Staff in Foca and then later the war commission, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was the president of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Petko Cancar, he was another of the Serb leaders in Foca, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did have a post or a function of some sort, but I don't know which. They were civilians, we were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic -- you say they were civilians, we were soldiers, during the period that it was Territorial Defence forces in Foca, Mr. Stanic was involved with those forces, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that Miroslav Stanic was the president of the Crisis Staff in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Once the VRS units were created, he and the other civilian authorities, they were civilians, you were soldiers, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm not sure. I don't know what function they had at the time because I never saw them in my vicinity.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not understand the last portion of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, could you perhaps repeat your answer for the benefit of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I was in the war. I fought as a Republika Srpska soldier. Now as to what role they played in the effort to establish the army, I don't know. The only thing I know is that Miroslav Stanic was the president of the Crisis Staff. I know Petko Cancar. But we soldiers, we did not care about their functions. At least I did not. I do know about Miroslav Stanic. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence that Serb leaders in Foca, including those two, openly discussed the departure of the great majority, almost all of the Muslims from Foca municipality. So Muslims continued leaving, including what you described as honest Muslims, long after the takeover in April, right?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
utterances.text: I have to apologise to this honourable Court. I did not say that these two made the Muslims leave Foca, as the Prosecutor put it to me, if I understand correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Perhaps there was a translation issue and so I'll suggest I'll just repeat my question, if that's acceptable. What I said was: The Chamber has received evidence from other witnesses, and from documents, that Serb leaders in Foca, including Mr. Stanic and Mr. Cancar, openly discussed the departure of the great majority, almost all, of the Muslims from Foca municipality. What they discussed happened, didn't it? Muslims continued leaving, including what you described as honest Muslims, long after April 1992?

utterances.speaker: VESELINKO SIMOVIC
